product.title: Pearl Harbor. 7 decembrie 1941, ziua care a schimbat cursul istoriei
product.description: În celebrul său discurs ținut în fața Congresului Statelor Unite, președintele Franklin D. Roosevelt a numit ziua de 7 decembrie 1941 „unul dintre cele mai infame momente ale istoriei“. Iar timpul a dovedit că a avut dreptate: în acea zi, bombardierele japoneze care au atacat baza americană de la Pearl Harbor au făcut 3 566 de victime (dintre care 2 388 de morți) și au scufundat sau avariat grav opt cuirasate, trei crucișătoare ușoare, patru distrugătoare și 350 de avioane. În mod paradoxal, atacul japonez nu a destabilizat SUA, ci le-a făcut mai puternice, ducând la sfârșitul Marii Crize economice și determinând intrarea lor în cel de-al Doilea Război Mondial. Istoricul Steven M. Gillon analizează evenimentele pline de tensiune și de emoție din primele 24 de ore de după atac, arătând modul în care președintele și publicul american au reacționat. Autorul oferă, în acest scop, o descriere plină de viață, minut de minut, a modului inteligent în care Roosevelt a gestionat situația. Hotărât și abil, președintele a reușit să inspire și să unească națiunea, ascunzând, în același timp, Congresului și publicului american proporțiile reale ale distrugerilor provocate de atac.   Steven M. Gillon este profesor de istorie la Universitatea din Oklahoma și un colaborator constant al History Channel. Este autorul a numeroase cărți și articole despre istoria și politica modernă a Statelor Unite, printre care The American Paradox: A History of the United States Since 1945 (2006), 10 Days That Unexpectedly Changed America (2006) și The Kennedy Assassination – 24 Hours After (2010).

# Pearl Harbor: December 7, 1941 â The Day That Changed the Course of History

Dive deep into one of the most pivotal moments in modern history with this comprehensive non-fiction account. *Pearl Harbor: December 7, 1941* chronicles not only the devastating attack but also the extraordinary resilience and leadership that followed. This book explores how an unexpected disaster transformed American resolve, ultimately determining the course of World War II.

If you are fascinated by major global conflicts, American political history, or the crucial moments of decision-making under pressure, this detailed analysis is essential reading.

***

## The Defining Day: Analyzing the Attack on Pearl Harbor

On December 7, 1941, a Japanese aerial attack struck the American base at Pearl Harbor. The sheer scale of the devastation was staggering: over 3,566 casualties (including 2,388 deaths) and massive damage to military assets, including eight battleships, three light cruisers, four destroyers, and 350 aircraft.

This account moves beyond simply recounting the tragedy; it analyzes the immediate aftermath. Historian Steven M. Gillon provides a tense, minute-by-minute narrative of the first 24 hours following the attack, detailing how both military and civilian life unfolded under immense pressure.

### The Paradoxical Strength: How Crisis Fueled America

The most compelling aspect of the story is the historical paradox: the Japanese attack, while devastating, did not destabilize the United States. Instead, the event served as a catalyst that helped end the Great Depression and propelled the nation into its role as a global superpower.

The book richly details the political maneuvering during this period, focusing on how President Franklin D. Roosevelt managed to unify a nation reeling from shock and loss. Learn how FDRâwith determination and skillâmanaged public perception while simultaneously inspiring the country toward strength and war effort.

## Expert Insights into American History

Authored by renowned history professor Steven M. Gillon, this book provides unmatched insight into the complex blend of emotion, strategy, and political governance that defined early 20th-century America. The narrative is highly readable, making complex geopolitical events accessible to all history enthusiasts.

**About the Author:**
Steven M. Gillon is a professor of history at the University of Oklahoma and a regular contributor to History Channel. He is an established authority on U.S. modern political and military history, having authored multiple acclaimed works, including *The American Paradox: A History of the United States Since 1945* (2006) and *10 Days That Unexpectedly Changed America* (2006).

***

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Q: Is this book focused purely on military strategy?**
A: No. While it heavily covers the naval attack, the focus is equally placed on political leadership. The author analyzes how President Roosevelt managed public opinion, rallied national support, and navigated the immediate diplomatic crisis that followed the Pearl Harbor incident.

**Q: Does this book cover the entire WWII period?**
A: The primary focus is the critical first 24 hours and the immediate impact of the attack leading up to America's full involvement in World War II. It provides the essential context for understanding how the war began.
